To: d.kerrigan@northmail.example
Replying to: m01
Cc: none
Subject: Re: Blister packs for my mother - new patient

Dear Mr. Kerrigan,

Thank you for contacting Erindale Park Pharmacy, and welcome. We would be glad to look after your mother's medications. I am sorry to hear about her fall, and I hope she continues to recover well at home.

Here are answers to your questions.

1. Blister packs and cost: Yes, we prepare weekly blister packs. Her medications are sealed into packets labelled for each day and each time of day (morning, noon, evening and bedtime), which should help with the mix-ups. There is no charge for the packaging itself. She would pay our normal dispensing fee for her prescriptions, and since she is over 65 the Ontario Drug Benefit program may cover most of that. We will confirm the exact amounts with you when we set up her file.

2. Delivery: Yes, we can deliver to her building. Our regular deliveries are on Tuesdays and Fridays between 2 and 6 p.m., and they are free within 8 km of the store, which includes Mississauga Valley. Because her discharge is on Thursday, the first packs will need to be picked up or delivered on a different day. For those, we can either hold them for pickup or I can arrange a one-off drop-off at her condo on Saturday before 1 p.m.

3. Moving her prescriptions: Please send me the name and address of her current pharmacy on Dundas, and her OHIP number. We will call them to transfer her profile and prescriptions. Your mother does not need to sign anything for the transfer. Her new prescriptions from the hospital are the other piece. Our first packs take about 48 hours to prepare once we have all of her prescriptions, so I would be grateful if you could ask the discharge team to fax them to us early Thursday morning. If they arrive then, her packs should be ready on Saturday.

4. Speaking with you about her medications: I would be happy to go through her new medication list with you. Before I can discuss her medications with anyone other than her, however, we need her permission. Our pharmacy records this with a Family Communication Consent form, which Margaret signs to tell us who she is comfortable having us speak with about her health. It is there to protect her privacy and to make sure she is always in control of her own information. Once it is signed, I am glad to take you through the full list. Because she is hard of hearing, I can also write her list out in large print and go over it with her in person so that she has it in front of her. She can sign the consent form when she collects her packs on Saturday, or we can bring it to her with our driver.

We also offer a MedsCheck after hospital discharge. It is a 20-minute review of her medications with the pharmacist, and it can be done in the store or at her home if she is not able to travel yet. I would like to offer to visit her at home in her first week back. I am free on Monday or Tuesday evening after 6 p.m. next week. Please let me know which evening suits you and your mother best.

Finally, since her first packs will not be ready on the day she leaves hospital, could you please check with the discharge team that she will have an interim supply of all her medications to take home on Thursday? It would also help a great deal if you could work with them to go through each dose with her until she has her packs on Saturday, so she does not miss anything or take the wrong dose in the meantime. Please let me know what they confirm and I will do the same on our end.

You can reach me directly at 905-555-0148, extension 2. I am in the store Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., so that is the best time to catch me. I look forward to looking after your mother.

Kind regards,

Rania Haddad
Pharmacist
Erindale Park Pharmacy
905-555-0148 ext. 2

reasons: The draft does not explicitly offer a telephone call to review the medication list.
